getting.where: Harmonic Camp on a dissonant planet
getting.how: Solve the sealed-cabinet puzzle at the camp terminal. Best tool available early.

getting.where: Space station cabinets in wealthy systems
getting.how: Wealthy systems have the highest S-class chance, and every station has two cabinets. Use the rotation trick.

sentinel_puzzle.title: The free S-class Sentinel tool, step by step
steps: Go to the camp's terminal, not the container.
Choose Scan Memory Registers - you get three addition problems, e.g. 4+11, 2+7, 3+1.
Choose Input Override Glyphs and enter the three answers (15, 9, 4). The glyphs are numbered.
Order does not matter - only the three correct numbers.
Deactivate the multi-tool seal, then take the tool from the container.
after: It arrives with broken nodes: repair with Radiant Shards and Atlantideum, the purple crystals on the same planet. Radiant Shards also refine to 50 nanites each.
At the 6 active tool cap you must exchange, not acquire - decide which one dies before walking in.
Strip the old tool first: Y (Xbox) / Triangle (PlayStation) on installed tech picks it back up, Terrain Manipulator included. You lose nothing by swapping.
The same dissonance spikes also mark crashed Sentinel ships, so stack the trip.

cabinet_trick.title: The cabinet rotation trick
steps: Visit a planet in the system.
Save and reload on the planet's surface.
Return to the space station - both cabinets have changed.
cabinet_trick.note: One cabinet pulls from the planetary pool, the other from the station's own rotation, which scales with the planet count. A six-planet system can offer up to 12 designs at one station.

hunting.title: Hunting a specific tool from a location guide
steps: Get to the right galaxy (for Eissentam: featured bases at the Anomaly, a hub player, or the Artemis questline's green choice).
Turn multiplayer OFF before you portal - the tool instance is shared, and if someone else grabs it first it is gone for everyone.
Look for a communication station marking the spot, or navigate to the published coordinates.
At the settlement, get out of your ship and reload the autosave that just triggered - the tool appears in the cabinet after the reload.
You still pay for it. The worked example cost 7.5 million units.

rules.title: Damage Potential is not damage output
rules.body: It rolls up the installed weapons and damage tech, including the mining beam, and you can only fire one weapon at a time. There is no DPS readout anywhere in the game; the only real measurement is shooting something and reading the numbers. It is still the best measuring stick you have - strip the loadout to one thing and add pieces one at a time to watch the delta.

rules.title: Adjacency runs horizontally and vertically, never diagonally
rules.body: Group same-weapon-type upgrades together; a coloured border means the bonus is live. The bonus takes the class of the lowest member of the pair, so an A next to an S gives an A-class bonus. Some upgrades give no adjacency at all - no border ever appears, so stop trying to fit them into the block.

rules.title: Supercharged slots want to be a 2x2 block
rules.body: Four in a square all feed each other because adjacency is horizontal and vertical only; four in a line or scattered do not. This is fixed at spawn and is the single thing that separates a great tool from an average one - it is what to look for when hunting.

rules.title: Supercharge the weapon itself
rules.body: The weapon shows no visible stats, so the slot looks wasted. Swapping the weapon out for an A-class upgrade dropped a loadout from 24,000 to 14,000. Worth testing yourself: this rests on the Damage Potential number, and part of the community argues the opposite.

rules.title: Put the Optical Drill in a supercharged slot
rules.body: It boosts efficiency by 88%, nearly doubling mining output - one of the strongest early upgrades in the game.

rules.title: Add the ordinary Mining Laser to a Sentinel tool
rules.body: Alongside the Sentinel's own laser it takes Damage Potential from 469 to 1,164 with no weapons installed, slows overheating and massively boosts mining.

rules.title: Scanner Range above ~700 is wasted
rules.body: The game does not display critical survival resources beyond roughly a 600-unit radius even with Scanner Range over 2,000.

rules.title: You do not need X-class
rules.body: X-class rolls come from pirate/outlaw station vendors and are a lottery - they can come out worse than C. The right tool with a good supercharged arrangement and the best S-class upgrades handles anything the game throws at you.

rules.title: Do not rush slot expansion
rules.body: Each slot costs progressively more, eventually 600 million units, and filling one tool with units alone runs past 10 billion. Saved Multi-tool Expansion Slots are worth hundreds of millions each. Upgrade class with nanites first: max slots are C 21, B 30, A 45, S 60.

rules.title: There is no need to chase a natural S-class
rules.body: Any tool upgrades to S at the station Upgrade Station with nanites. Pick a design you like and upgrade it yourself.

rules.title: You can hold 6 active and 18 archived
rules.body: The archive is reached through a Weapon Rack - buildable on a base, a corvette or a freighter. Salvage unwanted tools at the Anomaly's Decommissioning Terminal, which can even return Expansion Slots.
